extracted.intended_audience: museum professionals, grantmakers, program evaluators, and policymakers involved with IMLS Museums for America grants
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying the evaluation dimensions used in the IMLS Museums for America program evaluation to judge grant project outcomes (audience effects, programming continuity, organizational capacity, partnerships, digitization/accessibility, and sustainability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Serves external audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the grant project served external audiences versus museum staff only (Nearly all (94%) respondents indicated that their grant project served external audiences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects serving external audiences are counted as reaching communities; projects serving only staff were more likely to focus on Digitization/Collections or Organizational Development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience reach: specific population groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Which population groups the project reached (students, youth, families, low‑income communities, paid staff, unpaid/volunteers, professionals such as scholars, independent researchers, genealogists, adult and older student groups, children middle‑school or below).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report provides frequency examples (e.g., programming projects most frequently reached students (80%), youth (74%), and families (54%); Digitization/Collections reached museum staff paid (84%) and unpaid/volunteers (60%)). Use these categories to classify audience reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reached new audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Project expanded audience base to include new groups (e.g., youth, minorities, families) — measured as 'Reached new audiences' (73% reported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider both short-term and post-grant evidence (survey percentages, qualitative comments) of newly reached groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increased commitment by existing audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Project led to increased commitment or engagement by existing audiences (64% reported increased commitment by existing audiences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes indicators such as increased memberships, repeat visitation, greater usage, and deeper engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increased audience access to museum resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Project increased audience access through strategies such as expanded hours, mobile programming, online access, or unified searchable collections (46% reported increased access).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digitization and technology projects are especially likely to increase access; look for concrete access mechanisms (website redesign, online catalog, databases).

rubrics_metrics.name: No effect on audiences / audience effects not relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects that reported no audience effect or where audience effects were not relevant (e.g., many Digitization/Collections and Organizational Development projects indicated audience effects were not relevant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret 'no effect' in context — may reflect internal focus (research, asset management) rather than failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Success in sustaining new audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Self‑reported characterization of efforts to sustain new audiences (not at all successful / somewhat successful / very successful); 99% reported at least somewhat or very successful; 49% 'very successful'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these ordinal categories to assess longer‑term retention and sustainability of audience gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑grant longer‑term audience effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Longer‑term outcomes observed three or more years after project completion (e.g., reaching new audiences, increasing visitation, receiving more requests for materials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualitative comments provide examples of sustained effects and unanticipated evolutions (e.g., outreach replacing on‑site attendance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Engaging diverse and accessibility‑focused audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Design and implementation of inclusive practices to engage audiences with disabilities or special needs (examples: audio CDs, textured maps, Braille transcriptions, sign‑language interpreters, adapted exhibit interfaces such as cameras/monitors/sound tubes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess specific accessibility adaptations and evidence that they enabled participation (e.g., visitors could explore exhibit space despite physical impairments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Digitization/Collections effect on access and research
rubrics_metrics.description: Digitization projects' impact on public and professional access: unified collections, cross‑collection searchability, online public databases enabling genealogists/researchers to browse/search without librarian assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for evidence of increased requests, deeper engagement with collections, researchers' ability to draw connections, and user contributions to databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming continuation (sustaining/expanding programming)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether MFA programming continued after the grant: at least somewhat successful vs very successful (98% at least somewhat; 62% 'very successful'); 91% reported positive change in at least one programming area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disaggregate by project focus and award size (Technology-focused projects and larger awards reported higher continuation rates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanded range of programming or exhibit possibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Project expanded the range of possibilities for programs or exhibits the museum could undertake (64% reported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes new themes, formats, or capacities that enabled different or larger-scale programming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developed related programming
rubrics_metrics.description: Project produced related programming that expanded the value of the grant-funded work (58% reported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence includes new programs modeled on the grant project, spin-offs, or applying design concepts to subsequent exhibits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efforts to seek additional funding to sustain programming
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the museum sought additional funding to sustain grant-funded programming (nearly half did); frequency varies by grant size (larger grants more likely to seek additional funding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as an indicator of intention/effort to institutionalize programming beyond grant period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Did not sustain grant‑funded programming
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances where grant-funded programming was not sustained (small percentage, e.g., 5% in exhibit breakdown).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextual reasons include experimental trials, low attendance due to external changes, or intentional short-term 'springboard' projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of evaluation and experimental design in program development
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of front‑end evaluation, experimental design, pilot‑testing, formative evaluations, and attendance numbers to shape program content and decide continuation (e.g., Project Curiosity, Watershed Moments employed front‑end evaluation and experimental design).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether projects used evidence to iterate formats and messages, including formative/follow‑up studies measuring behavior change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability via institutionalization and diversified funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Pathways to sustain project outcomes: incorporation into operating budgets, additional IMLS or other agency/foundation funding, corporate sponsorships, or partnerships (examples given where projects were written into operating budgets or secured other funding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for explicit evidence of budgetary adoption, continuing staffing, or secured alternate funding sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational capacity: strengthened museum profile/public image
rubrics_metrics.description: Project effects on museum reputation: strengthened public image (80% reported) and strengthened museum profile in the community (89% reported at least one community effect).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes community awareness, professional recognition, and media coverage as components of reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational capacity: increased visibility as center of community learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Project increased institution's visibility as a center of community learning (64% reported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider evidence of educational role amplification and public perception shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational capacity: raised prestige in community
rubrics_metrics.description: Project raised institution's prestige in its community (59% reported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prestige may be linked to subsequent funding opportunities and partnerships; small museums reported larger relative prestige gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational capacity: increased local media coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Project resulted in local media coverage of institution's activities (42% reported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media coverage is an indicator of public visibility and profile-building effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational identity change
rubrics_metrics.description: Project led to changes in institutional identity (23% reported), e.g., redefined mission emphasis or public role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess depth of identity change — framing, strategic plan inclusion, or shifts in programmatic priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership effects: raised community awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Partnerships formed in connection with the project raised community awareness of the museum (Exhibit IV‑7: 76% of projects involving partners).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partnerships are counted when they demonstrably increased reach/awareness beyond what the museum could achieve alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership effects: brought in new audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Partnerships helped bring in new audiences (66% of projects involving partners).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether partners opened access to constituencies the museum previously did not reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership effects: brought in new resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Partnerships provided access to new resources not otherwise available (48% reported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources include funding, in‑kind support, facilities, expertise, or materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership effects: brought in new staff (paid or unpaid)
rubrics_metrics.description: Partnerships contributed new staff, paid or unpaid (32% reported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes volunteers, interns, or partner‑provided personnel supporting the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership effects: brought in new memberships
rubrics_metrics.description: Partnerships led to new memberships (22% reported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership gains are an indicator of sustained audience engagement and institutional support.

rubrics_metrics.name: No effect due to partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Some partnered projects reported no measurable partnership effects (small percentage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of effect should be interpreted alongside partnership design and mutual goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership building: strengthened ongoing partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects strengthened ongoing partnerships (70% of partnered projects reported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengthening may be evidenced by continued collaboration, formalized agreements, or joint initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership building: developed new partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects developed new partnerships (62% reported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New partnerships expand institutional networks and future project capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership building: improved partnership‑building skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects improved respondents' skills in building partnerships (53% reported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skill gains include learning processes for sustaining relationships and identifying mutual goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership building: increased ability to attract more partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects increased institutions' ability to attract more partners (44% reported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Larger grants and project visibility appear associated with greater ability to attract partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership building: developed new types of partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects led to development of new types of partnerships (36% reported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New partnership types may include cross‑sector collaborations or partnerships for distinct purposes (education, conservation, research).

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence of museum size and grant size on outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcome frequencies differ by museum size (small, medium, large) and grant size (small, medium, large): e.g., small museums reported greater profile impacts; larger grants correlated with increased audience commitment and higher rates of seeking additional funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stratified analysis by museum and grant size to interpret effect magnitudes and target supports appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity building: staff professional development and credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects produced staff capacity gains (e.g., staff became credentialed youth development specialists; professional development increased appreciation/skills).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess training, credentialing, and staff role changes tied to project activities as markers of institutional capacity growth.
